readings: The interface has no data input, so the 'proper bit pattern' cannot be detected; implement only the reset-triggered 4-cycle shift_ena and ignore pattern detection.
Assume an external pattern-detect signal exists but is omitted from the interface, so the module's behavior depends on an unseen signal.
shift_ena is asserted for 4 cycles starting immediately after the clock edge where reset is sampled, and if reset stays high, shift_ena remains high (or restarts) beyond 4 cycles.
shift_ena is asserted for exactly 4 cycles beginning the cycle after reset is deasserted; during reset assertion shift_ena is 0 (or don't care) and does not count toward the 4.
After the reset-initiated 4-cycle sequence, shift_ena stays 0 forever regardless of any pattern; the word 'whenever' is contradictory or only refers to reset.
After the reset-initiated sequence, detection of the proper pattern can trigger additional 4-cycle shift_ena sequences without reset.
The 'proper bit pattern' is a specific sequence (e.g., 1101) defined elsewhere; the implementer must guess it.
The 'proper bit pattern' is any pattern matching a condition; without a defined input or pattern, detection is undefined and may be omitted.
